annotations.text:
CURRICULUM BOOKSHELF — settled
Four boards: the top three split in two, the bottom one whole. Seven bays, a year to each, every book standing at once, so the accordion and the two arches become one object.
Each bay is a wooden frame around a recessed green well with a brass year plate screwed to its bottom rail. Clicking a spine turns that book face-on in its own slot; nothing opens anywhere else on the page. Timings and fees sit above the shelf as mounted plates, each part divided by a short gold rule.
Live — click a spine. Second Year holds the real books; every other bay is a dashed TODO slot on purpose, awaiting content from the masjid.

Carried into the build
· Wood is the ground's own edge-shading hue (rgba(122,96,54) on body) at furniture weight, #4a3a22 — the one value here not already in :root. Grain is a repeating-linear-gradient, no image to maintain.
· The turned book is 268×182 and holds a title, the Urdu, a subject and about two sentences. Book descriptions in curriculum.json need to stay near that length.
· The bottom bay is mostly empty — one year across the full width leaves bare board. Seventh Year's slots are centred rather than stretched.
· Still open for the build: what the four rows do below ~880px, and keyboard order across 42 spines (the accordion's tablist pattern does not survive a 2-D grid unchanged).

STUDIES — kept for the record, not for the build
Top row: the two unchosen year-plate treatments. Below: the five original placement studies, which still carry the bookend plate and gold shelf boards the framed version replaces.

B · Plaque as lintel
Frames hung on the ground with no cabinet, plate straddling the top rail.
Why not: with nothing holding them together the seven bays stop reading as one bookshelf.

C · Plaque on the stile
One carcass, bays routed out of it, plate a vertical strip on the left stile.
Why not: the 46px stile costs every bay 33px, and VII · SEVENTH YEAR set vertically was already at its size ceiling.

1 · Lectern — panel under the whole shelf
Why not: a top-row book moves the text ~900px away, with nothing in between to carry the eye.

2 · Shelf drawer — opens in its own row
Why not: the shelf changes height on every click — the same complaint the accordion already has.

3 · Facing page — shelf left, open book right
Why not: a permanent 400px column, and no mobile form under ~880px.

4 · Pulled from the shelf — CHOSEN
The spine turns face-on in its own slot. Carried forward on the Bookshelf page, where the bookend plate became a plate on the frame.

5 · Popover — the book speaks where it stands
Why not: it covers neighbouring books, needs a dismiss affordance and a focus-trap answer, and has to flip sides near a bay edge.
